title: Each part of a plan ruling cites its step, a check flags a missing one, and the re-rank agent reads plan against roadmap
why: A ruling's part can drop with no step and nobody sees it: R28's one-store part had none until page-data-one-store.
source: owner 11:31 CST Nov 12 in chat, relayed by the retrospective (session_013NEJKz5AWFJhGvmCUoi6wQ) 11:32 CST, page item 555 ruling-parts-to-steps: "probably both is fine -- and note that the id's probably need good tagging right slugs or whatever or that won't matter here?"
note: Both parts ruled. (a) Each numbered part of a plan ruling names its step as step:<slug>; an opaque id (239 of 1,529 steps, such as c55) carries a short gloss; a check on the plan, at each push, flags a part with no step or a cited step that no longer exists, and accepts either form. (b) The agent from step queue-score-plus-agent reads the plan's rulings against the steps at each batch merge and files what is missing. Home: decision session-tiers, beside queue-score-plus-agent. The retrospective adds step ids to the plan's ruling parts as it writes them. Part (b) waits on queue-score-plus-agent. Ready, no lane. Lane ruling-parts-cite-steps started 11:34 CST Nov 12 (coordinator), part a only; part b waits on queue-score-plus-agent. Triage duty (lane note 3, 12:38 CST Nov 12): deleting, renaming or folding a step that a plan part cites turns CI red on the next push; re-cite the new slug in the plan in the same act.
